caption: Active filters against the passive shapes from the General course. Each panel draws the passive prototype (dotted: a single RC low-pass or high-pass, a single-tuned band-pass hump) beside two active 2nd-order stages: Q = 0.7 (dash-dot, maximally flat, the Butterworth member of the pool's filter ladder) and Q = 4 (solid, peaking). The active lessons: each reactive section adds 6 dB per octave, so the two-pole active stage falls at 40 dB/decade where the passive RC manages 20, and a high Q lifts the corner above 0 dB - peaking - while an active stage can add real passband gain besides (every curve here is normalized so the shapes compare). In the band-pass panel the same Q law reads as a narrower window, BW = f0/Q. The pool ties: Butterworth is maximally flat, Chebyshev trades passband ripple for a sharper cutoff, and the elliptical filter is sharpest with stop-band notches (E7C05, E7C06); shape factor measures adjacent-channel rejection (E7C11); and a capacitor across RF in Figure E7-3 turns the inverting op-amp into exactly the low-pass shape in the first panel (E7G02).
spoken: Three response panels - low-pass, high-pass, band-pass - plotting relative response in dB against frequency normalized to f0 on a log scale from a tenth to ten times f0. In every panel a dotted passive curve, a dash-dot active curve with Q of 0.7, and a solid active curve with Q of 4. In the low-pass panel the passive RC falls gently at 20 dB per decade while the active curves fall at 40, and the Q of 4 curve peaks above plus 12 dB at the corner, marked peaking: Q lifts the corner above 0 dB. The high-pass panel mirrors it. In the band-pass panel all curves peak at 0 dB at f0, and higher Q simply narrows the window: bandwidth equals f0 over Q. A footnote gives the pool's filter ladder - Butterworth maximally flat, Chebyshev passband ripple with sharper cutoff, elliptical sharpest with stop-band notches - and notes that a capacitor across R F in Figure E7-3 makes the low-pass shape.
